newsitem.title: DENMARK: Dollar-sensitive Danish stocks push index to high.
newsitem.headline: Dollar-sensitive Danish stocks push index to high.

text.p: The top-20 Danish KFX share index closed at an all-time record high for the eleventh consecutive trading day on Tuesday and dealers foresaw another record day ahead on Wednesday regardless of foreign trends.
"It was Moeller, Tele Danmark and Novo Nordisk, which pulled the index up," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.86 point higher at 187.96. The KFX August future rose 1.30 point to 188.70 with 759 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Dollar-sensitive paper had a field day with Novo Nordisk putting on 20 crowns to close at 770, while Moeller's D/S Svendborg rose 7,000 crowns to finish at 401,000 and twin D/S 1912 ended 4,000 up at 279,000.
Moeller's Maersk Oil and Gas unit's oil production in Qatar is exceeding expectations and, like its shipping operations, benefitting from the higher value of its dollar earnings.
Novo benefitted from a pharmacy-sector rise after strong first-half results from Switzerland's Roche.
